classification.difficultyReason: Identify sign changes and calculate separate positive areas using polynomial antiderivatives.

content.prompt: In each part, find the area of the region bounded by the graph of the function and the $x$-axis between the specified values. Areas above and below the $x$-axis must be calculated separately. A sketch of the curve will help.

answer.worked:
$y=x^2\geq0$, so the entire region is above the $x$-axis.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=\int_{-3}^{2}x^2\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{-3}^{2}\\&=\frac83-(-9)\\&=\frac{35}{3}=11\frac23\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

The zero is $x=0$. The curve is below the $x$-axis on $[-4,0]$ and above it on $[0,1]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{below}}&=-\int_{-4}^{0}2x^3\,dx\\&=-\left[\frac{x^4}{2}\right]_{-4}^{0}\\&=-(0-128)=128.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{above}}&=\int_{0}^{1}2x^3\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^4}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}\\&=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
$$A=128+\frac12=128\frac12\text{ units}^2.$$

The zeros are $x=0$ and $x=2$. The curve is below the $x$-axis on $(0,2)$.
$$\begin{aligned}A&=-\int_0^2(3x^2-6x)\,dx\\&=-[x^3-3x^2]_0^2\\&=-[(8-12)-0]\\&=4\text{ units}^2.\end{aligned}$$

The zero is $x=3$. The curve is below the $x$-axis on $[-1,3]$ and above it on $[3,4]$.
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{below}}&=-\int_{-1}^{3}(x-3)\,dx\\&=-\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-3x\right]_{-1}^{3}\\&=-\left[\left(\frac92-9\right)-\left(\frac12+3\right)\right]\\&=8.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{above}}&=\int_3^4(x-3)\,dx\\&=\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-3x\right]_3^4\\&=(8-12)-\left(\frac92-9\right)=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
$$A=8+\frac12=8\frac12\text{ units}^2.$$

$y=x^3-7x+6$, with zeros at $x=-3,1,2$.
On $(-3,1)$, checking $x=0$ gives $y=6>0$, so the curve is above the $x$-axis. On $(1,2)$, checking $x=1.5$ gives $y=-1.125<0$, so it is below.
$$F(x)=\frac{x^4}{4}-\frac{7x^2}{2}+6x.$$
$$F(-3)=-\frac{117}{4},\qquad F(1)=\frac{11}{4},\qquad F(2)=2.$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{above}}&=F(1)-F(-3)\\&=\frac{11}{4}+\frac{117}{4}\\&=32.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}A_{\text{below}}&=-[F(2)-F(1)]\\&=-\left[2-\frac{11}{4}\right]\\&=\frac34.\end{aligned}$$
$$A=32+\frac34=32\frac34\text{ units}^2.$$

$y=-2x(x+1)=-2x^2-2x$, with zeros at $x=-1$ and $x=0$.
On $(-2,-1)$, checking $x=-1.5$ gives $y=-1.5$, below the $x$-axis. On $(-1,0)$, checking $x=-0.5$ gives $y=0.5$, above. On $(0,2)$, checking $x=1$ gives $y=-4$, below.
$$F(x)=-\frac{2x^3}{3}-x^2.$$
$$F(-2)=\frac43,\quad F(-1)=-\frac13,\quad F(0)=0,\quad F(2)=-\frac{28}{3}.$$
Below on $[-2,-1]$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_1&=-[F(-1)-F(-2)]\\&=-\left[-\frac13-\frac43\right]=\frac53.\end{aligned}$$
Above on $[-1,0]$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_2&=F(0)-F(-1)\\&=0-\left(-\frac13\right)=\frac13.\end{aligned}$$
Below on $[0,2]$:
$$\begin{aligned}A_3&=-[F(2)-F(0)]\\&=-\left[-\frac{28}{3}-0\right]=\frac{28}{3}.\end{aligned}$$
$$A=\frac53+\frac13+\frac{28}{3}=\frac{34}{3}\text{ units}^2.$$
